The task in this study is social decision-making/uncertainty integration (making second guesses based on social vs individual information) rather than a problem-solving task as defined in I5 (goal-directed planning/sequencing/executing operations to arrive at a novel solution). The document does satisfy other inclusion criteria: whole-brain group-level BOLD analyses in healthy adults with reported stereotactic (MNI) peak coordinates. No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, not between-group-only, not a non-empirical paper). Therefore exclude because it fails I5 (problem-solving task).

This study reports task-based fMRI BOLD contrasts where participants performed mental transformation tasks (mental transposition and melody reversal) that require a goal (judge whether second melody matches a transformed version) and application of rule-based operations to reach that goal—meeting the review’s definition of problem-solving. It includes whole-brain, group-level analyses in healthy adult participants (n=12), reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space, and provides voxelwise coordinate results (tables of peaks). No exclusion criteria are met (analyses are not ROI-only, include within-group task effects in healthy adults). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied.

The study used a task-based neuroimaging paradigm (serial subtraction mental arithmetic) that requires goal-directed operations and rule-based execution, meeting the review's definition of problem solving (I5). It reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses in healthy adults (separate within-group effects for males and females and between-group contrasts), satisfying I6. Results are given in MNI space with reported peak coordinates (Table 1), satisfying I7. The measure is regional cerebral blood flow (perfusion/rCBF), satisfying I8. Voxelwise results are reported in figures and tables, meeting I9. No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are whole-brain (not ROI-only), include within-group healthy task effects (not only between-group or demographic-only contrasts), and the paper is empirical human data. Full text is available in the provided record (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study is excluded because it does not meet the review’s requirement that the paper report whole-brain task effects in healthy adult participants for a problem-solving task. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (study reports only between-group contrasts and within-patient ROI comparisons and does not report any healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (results reported in MNI coordinate space), I8 (BOLD fMRI measure reported), I9 (voxelwise/peak results reported as stereotactic peaks). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is an Operation Span working-memory/word-recognition task, which does not meet the review’s definition of a problem-solving task), I6 (no whole-brain analysis reporting group-level task effects in healthy adults—the only whole-brain result is a between-group contrast KLS>controls). Therefore the paper must be excluded.

The study reports two within-group contrasts (Internet Task > control; Book Task > control) in healthy older adults with whole-brain random-effects BOLD analyses and stereotactic (MNI) peak coordinates (meets I6, I7, I8, I9). However, the tasks do not clearly meet the review’s definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The Internet Task is described as an information search/visual search task (“obtain information on a specific topic”) and the Book Task is reading simulated pages; neither description provides evidence of engagement in explicit problem-solving processes as defined (identifying/planning/sequencing operations, applying rule-based operations to arrive at a novel solution). Because I5 is not satisfied, the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

Although this is an empirical, whole-brain BOLD fMRI study reporting stereotactic coordinates (MNI) of task-related activations for a mental-arithmetic task (meets I5, I7, I8, I9), it is a single-case study (n=1) of a 16-year-old participant. The review requires group-level effects in healthy adult individuals (I6). This study does not provide group-level analyses nor healthy adult participants (participant age mean 16), so it fails I6 and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are specifically met.

The study does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined in I5: the tasks involve reading poetic and prosaic texts and rating poeticness/reappraisal, not goal-directed problem solving that requires planning/sequencing actions or executing rule-based operations to reach a solution. It does meet other methodological criteria: whole-brain group-level BOLD analyses with stereotactic (MNI) coordinates are reported. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

Excluded because the paper reports only region-of-interest (ROI) analyses and no whole-brain group-level voxelwise results (Exclusion E3). Additionally, the task is a theory-of-mind/false-belief social cognition task, not a problem-solving task as defined in I5 (no evidence of goal-directed problem-solving operations, planning/sequencing, or rule-based solution execution). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (coordinates reported in MNI), I8 (BOLD fMRI measure reported), I9 (results reported in tables of coordinates). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving task as defined) and I6 (no whole-brain group-level analysis; model fit and inference restricted to ROIs). fulltext_incomplete=false.

The task is a discard/keep decision about personal vs experimenter possessions (emotionally-laden decision-making about ownership), which does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5 not met). The paper does report whole-brain BOLD analyses and stereotactic (MNI) coordinates (I7, I8, I9 met). However, it does not report a whole-brain, within-group task effect specifically for healthy adults; most reported whole-brain results are omnibus/between-group effects or within-group correlations in patients, so it fails the requirement for a healthy-group task effect (E5 applies; I6 not met). Therefore the study should be excluded.

This study does not meet the review’s definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The task is consumer information search/personal involvement (choose whether to continue collecting info for products), which lacks required elements of problem solving as defined (explicit goal-directed planning/sequencing and rule-based operations to arrive at a correct or previously unknown solution). The study does satisfy other methodological criteria: whole-brain group-level analysis reported (Analysis 2; I6), stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (I7), BOLD measure (I8), and voxelwise results reported in tables/peaks (I9). No exclusion criteria are triggered (e.g., it does not report only ROI results). Therefore the study is excluded because I5 is not met. Full text appears complete for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The task in this study is an event-related causality-judgement/perception task (judging whether animated collisions imply causality), not a problem-solving task as defined by I5 (no goal-directed planning, sequencing of actions, or execution of rule-based operations to reach a solution). The record shows whole-brain analyses (model fit over whole brain), BOLD measures, and stereotactic coordinates in MNI, and includes group-level effects involving healthy participants, so I6, I7, I8 and I9 are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study is excluded because it does not meet I5.

This study does not meet the review objective of whole-brain task-based fMRI studies of problem-solving in healthy adults. Specifically: (a) Inclusion criteria met: I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI305), I8 (reports BOLD fMRI results), I9 (voxelwise results/peaks reported in tables). (b) Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is the Ultimatum Game — a social fairness/decision-making task, not a defined problem-solving task per the review definition), I6 (no whole-brain group-level analysis reported that isolates or tests effects in a healthy adult-only group; analyses are across mixed age groups and/or regressions with age). (c) Exclusion criteria met: E5 (the paper does not provide a healthy adult-group task effect isolated for inclusion; analyses focus on between-group/age effects and developmental regressions). Therefore the paper is not eligible for the meta-analysis.

This study is excluded because it does not examine problem-solving in healthy adults. It uses a Cue Reactivity Task in a sample of alcohol-dependent patients (no healthy control group/task effect in healthy adults), so it violates E5. Although it reports stereotactic coordinates (MNI) and BOLD results (I7, I8) and lists peaks (I9), it does not meet I5 (not a problem-solving task) nor I6 (no whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adult individuals). Full text appears complete for screening.

(a) Exclusion IDs met: none.
(b) Inclusion IDs met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported via group analysis and reported peaks), I7 (stereotactic coordinates in Talairach), I8 (BOLD fMRI measure), I9 (results reported as coordinate peaks/tables).
(c) Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (the task is a working-memory training/matching task, not a problem-solving task as defined: it requires remembering locations/order and matching probes rather than goal-directed problem solving, planning/sequencing to reach a novel solution).
Detailed rationale: The paper reports task-based BOLD fMRI with group analyses and stereotactic peak coordinates in healthy adults, so it meets criteria I6–I9. However, the experimental task is a working memory/matching task (recall and probe matching) rather than a problem-solving task involving planning, evaluating, or executing operations to reach a goal as specified in I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Thus the study is excluded because it does not meet I5.

The study used a task (Operation Span) that includes execution of arithmetic operations and judgments (rule-based problem operations) while maintaining items, meeting the definition of problem-solving-related operations. It reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD fMRI analyses (multiple contrasts with model fit and inference over the whole brain), stereotactic coordinates in MNI space, and peak tables. Participants are healthy adults (n=25). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not between-group-only, not a review). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I9 are satisfied.

The study reports whole-brain, task-based BOLD fMRI results in healthy adults (Talairach coordinates) but the task does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task. The experimental tasks are training/recognition of novel symbols and numerical comparison (mapping symbols to approximate dot quantities), which are associative learning and magnitude-comparison/perceptual-decision tasks rather than goal-directed problem solving involving planning, sequencing, or executing operations within a rule set to reach a previously unknown solution. Thus inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task) is not met. The paper satisfies I6, I7, I8, and I9. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

The study reports a task-based fMRI study using a Mental Arithmetic Task (a problem-solving task involving numeric operations to arrive at correct sums), with healthy adult participants. It includes whole-brain, group-level (second-level random effects) analyses, reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (peaks/tables), and measures BOLD response. These map to inclusion criteria I5 (problem-solving/arithmetic task), I6 (whole-brain group-level effects), I7 (MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD), and I9 (coordinates reported in tables). No exclusion criteria are met. The NeuroStore record shows whole-brain within-group and between-group contrasts and reported peak coordinates, so the study is eligible for inclusion.

The study uses a risky decision-making (card-guessing/gambling) task rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (i.e., goal-directed planning/sequencing or executing rule-based operations to reach a correct/novel solution). It does satisfy other required criteria: whole-brain, group-level analyses in healthy adults (n=23) (I6); reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (I7); uses BOLD fMRI measures (I8); and voxelwise results are reported in tables (I9). It therefore fails inclusion criterion I5 (task is not a problem-solving task). No exclusion criteria are triggered (no ROI-only reporting, not only between-group/disease/age/gender comparisons, and is empirical). Full text is available in the provided record. Consequently the study is excluded.

This study is excluded because it does not include healthy adult task effects: participants are patients/familial high risk of schizophrenia and analyses are reported for patient groups only, therefore meeting exclusion criterion E5. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (results reported in MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI measure reported), and I9 (stereotactic results/peaks are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (does not include a whole-brain group-level effect in healthy adult individuals), and I5 (the Hayling Sentence Completion Test is a language/executive/response-selection task and the report does not clearly meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task). Full text is available in the NeuroStore record. Consequently the study is excluded.

Excluded because the task is a two-digit magnitude comparison (select the larger of two Arabic numbers), which does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5): it lacks multi-step planning, sequencing, or critical-evaluation operations to derive a previously unknown solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level analyses in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported in Talairach), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only reporting, no between-group-only contrasts, and the study is empirical with healthy participants). Therefore exclude for failing I5. Full text completeness: false = article document was available and readable, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This fMRI study does not meet the review objective for problem solving. It used a false-belief perspective-taking task (emotional vs cognitive perspective-taking), not a problem-solving task as defined in I5. Importantly, all reported analyses were ROI-based (Model fit over: region of interest; region-level thresholding), so no whole-brain voxelwise group analysis is available, violating I6 and meeting exclusion E3. The paper does report stereotactic coordinates in MNI (I7) and BOLD responses (I8), and coordinates are provided in tables (I9). However because it is ROI-only and not a problem-solving task, it must be excluded.

The study is a whole-brain, task-based fMRI experiment in healthy adults that reports BOLD coordinate results in standardized space, but it does not test a problem-solving task as defined by the review. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain random-effects analysis in healthy adults; n=16), I7 (reported stereotactic coordinates in MNI), I8 (BOLD fMRI measure), I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 — the task requires participants to identify 'how' or 'why' familiar actions (social/action knowledge judgment), not to pursue a goal and devise/plan/execute operations to reach a solution or perform critical-thinking problem solving. No exclusion criteria are otherwise triggered. Therefore the study is excluded for failing I5.

Excluded because the task does not meet the review's definition of problem solving (I5). The study presented captions that provided interpretations (humorous or nonhumorous) rather than requiring participants to engage in goal-directed problem solving, planning/sequencing actions, or executing rule-based operations to arrive at a solution. It does meet the other inclusion criteria: I6 (whole-brain, group-level random-effects analysis in healthy adults), I7 (coordinates reported in Talairach), I8 (BOLD fMRI measure), and I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables). No exclusion criteria were triggered (e.g., not ROI-only). Therefore excluded for failure to satisfy I5 (problem-solving task).

This study meets the review objective and all inclusion criteria: the tasks include executive/reasoning and rule-based prediction components consistent with problem-solving (I5); analyses are whole-brain random-effects group-level GLMs in healthy adults (I6); stereotactic coordinates are reported in Talairach space with tables of peak coordinates (I7); the measured signal is BOLD (functional) (I8); voxelwise results are provided in tables/peaks (I9). Participants are healthy adults and within-group task effects are reported for both experiments. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not only between-group/disease comparisons, and empirical human data). Full text appears complete in this derived record. Inclusion is appropriate.

The task involves instruction-based learning of arbitrary stimulus–response mappings requiring participants to apply an explicit rule set to produce correct responses (i.e., a goal-directed rule implementation), which meets the review's problem-solving definition (I5). The study reports whole-brain, group-level SPM analyses in healthy adult participants (n=16) (I6). Results are reported as voxel coordinates in MNI space (I7) and use BOLD fMRI measures (I8). Voxelwise peak tables are provided (acceptable per I9). No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are whole-brain (not ROI-only), involve a healthy-group task effect, and are empirical. Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

Excluded because the study reports only region-of-interest analyses (E3). The paper does meet some inclusion criteria: I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (coordinate results reported/available). However it fails I6 (does not include any whole-brain group-level analysis) because model fitting and inference were restricted to an a priori SN/VTA ROI. Therefore it does not meet all required inclusion criteria and is excluded.

The study is excluded because it does not demonstrate reporting of stereotactic coordinates in the provided document. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task appears to be a rule-based problem-solving task: subjects applied learned hierarchical/fractal rules to select the correct image), I6 (group whole-brain analysis reported with healthy adult participants, n=40), I8 (BOLD/fMRI measure reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (the document does not report task-related increases as stereotactic coordinates in Talairach or MNI space—only notes ‘Reported peaks: 1’ without coordinates or space), I9 (the record does not explicitly indicate that voxelwise coordinates are available in tables/figures/supplementary material). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore, per the requirement that all inclusion criteria must be satisfied, the study must be excluded. Full text is complete as provided (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study reports a task labeled as a Mental Arithmetic Task (magnitude comparison: indicate larger of two numbers), which constitutes a goal-directed numerical problem-solving operation that requires applying a rule-based operation to arrive at a correct response. It includes whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses in healthy adults (n=24), reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space with tabulated peak results, and uses BOLD fMRI. Whole-brain contrasts (Ar>Rest, Ng>Rest, Ng>Ar) and voxelwise FDR-thresholded analyses are reported. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9) and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of complex mental calculations that require goal setting, subgoal decomposition, planning/sequencing and rule-based operations—meeting the review's definition of problem solving (I5). It conducted whole-brain model fits and group-level analyses in healthy adults (n=14, ages 19–26), satisfying whole-brain group analysis requirement (I6). Results are reported in Talairach space with reported peak coordinates (tables) (I7) and the measured signal is BOLD (I8). Voxelwise exploratory analyses and coordinate tables are provided (I9). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, involves healthy participants, not a review). Given these points, the paper meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

The study does not examine a problem-solving task as defined. It uses N-back working memory and verbal fluency tasks, which involve working memory/update and lexical retrieval rather than goal-directed problem solving (planning/sequencing operations to reach a solution). The paper meets other neuroimaging criteria (whole-brain, group-level BOLD results reported in MNI coordinates and peaks in tables), but fails inclusion criterion I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore excluded for not meeting I5.

This study does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The task is an everyday moral decision/moral judgment paradigm involving choices between moral and hedonistic options; it assesses moral evaluation and emotional responses rather than goal-directed problem solving that requires planning/sequencing or executing operations to arrive at a solution. It does meet other inclusion criteria: whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults (I6), stereotactic MNI coordinates reported (I7), BOLD measure reported (I8), and voxelwise results available in tables/figures (I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore excluded because inclusion criterion I5 is not satisfied.

Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain analysis in healthy adults — model fit over whole brain and group-level effects reported, n=15), I7 (coordinates reported in Talairach), I8 (BOLD fMRI measures reported), I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (unclear/not met) — the task is an affective decision-making aviation task (decide to land or abort) under uncertainty and financial incentive; while goal-directed, it primarily probes perceptual/affective decision-making and risk/reward processing rather than explicit problem-solving as defined (requiring identification/planning/sequencing operations to arrive at a correct or novel solution). Because I5 is not satisfied, the study must be excluded from the problem-solving meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study using a mental rotation task in healthy adults that requires subjects to determine the location/orientation of an object after an imagined transformation (a goal-directed operation requiring execution of transformation rules). The study reports whole-brain group-level BOLD analyses (group t maps), stereotactic coordinates in MNI, and voxelwise results in tables/peaks. These features satisfy the meta-analysis inclusion criteria: task qualifies as problem-solving per the definition (goal + executing rule-based operations to arrive at a correct answer), whole-brain group-level analysis present, BOLD measure reported, and coordinates in MNI. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; includes within-group healthy-task effects).

This study does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (Inclusion I5). The task is verb generation (semantic language production), which involves retrieval/lexical access rather than goal-directed problem solving, planning/sequencing, or rule-based operations to arrive at a solution as defined. It does meet other inclusion criteria: whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults (I6), reports stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space (I7), reports BOLD responses (I8), and provides voxelwise results in tables (I9). No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., ROI-only, disease-only comparisons, or absence of healthy-group task effects). Therefore the paper is excluded because I5 is not satisfied.

The study employed a goal-directed route-planning task that required participants to choose and plan routes to a goal (planning/sequencing to reach a goal = problem solving). It is a task-based fMRI study using BOLD measures, with whole-brain, second-level random-effects analyses reported for healthy adult participants (n=18). Results are reported as stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (tables of peaks). These facts meet all required inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are met (analyses are whole-brain, not ROI-only; participants are healthy adults; empirical group-level task effects are reported).

The study reports a task-based fMRI investigation of decision-making in Prisoner’s Dilemma and Stag Hunt games that the authors explicitly describe as requiring "computational reasoning to derive the optimal solution," which fits the review's problem-solving definition (goal-directed reasoning, planning/evaluating to arrive at an optimal choice). It includes a whole-brain, group-level GLM with inference over the whole brain (n=23 healthy adults), reports BOLD responses, and provides stereotactic coordinates (Talairach) in a table. Therefore it meets I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

Although the study includes a serial arithmetic (Math) task, all reported voxelwise results are for the Story > Math contrast (narrative comprehension > arithmetic). The paper does not report coordinates for Math > Story (i.e., task-related increases associated with the problem-solving/arithmetic condition). The review objective requires studies that examine problem-solving and provide task-related activations for that process. Therefore this record does not provide usable problem-solving activation coordinates. Met inclusion criteria I6 (whole-brain group analysis in healthy adults), I7 (coordinates reported in Talairach space), I8 (BOLD analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results available). Did NOT meet I5 (does not report problem-solving-related activations/contrast). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete for the purposes of this screening.

This study does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by inclusion criterion I5. The task is social comparison (deciding whether one is taller or more intelligent than known individuals), which involves evaluative judgment rather than goal-directed problem solving, planning/sequencing actions, or executing rule-based operations to arrive at a solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level random-effects analysis in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in Talairach), I8 (BOLD fMRI measure), I9 (voxelwise results reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving paradigm). No exclusion criteria apply (EXCLUSION array: none). Full text is complete in the supplied record. Therefore the study is excluded for failing to meet I5.

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults reporting BOLD results in MNI space; however, the task assesses Theory of Mind/social cognition (video-based MASC false-belief inferences and implicit/explicit mental state reasoning), not problem-solving as defined by the review (goal-directed evaluation, planning/sequencing actions, or rule-based solution operations). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. It meets I6 (whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (coordinates in MNI), I8 (BOLD analysis), and I9 (coordinate reporting). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete in this record (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study meets all inclusion criteria: (I5) Tasks (number bisection, number comparison, mental arithmetic) require goal-directed rule-based operations and problem-solving (deciding means, comparing magnitudes), (I6) whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference are reported with group-level effects in adult participants (HMA vs LMA and within-group analyses), (I7) results reported in MNI coordinate space with reported peaks/tables, (I8) measure is BOLD fMRI, and (I9) stereotactic coordinate results/peaks are provided (tables). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only (E3), not limited to disease/age/gender comparisons (E4), and the paper includes within-group task effects in healthy adults (so it is not limited to only between-group contrasts; E5 not met). The NeuroStore labeling of ‘patients’ refers to the high/low math-anxiety groups but the document indicates healthy adult participants matched for performance, consistent with inclusion. Full text appears available in the provided record.

The study does not investigate a problem-solving task (I5 not met). The reported task is flickering checkerboard stimulation with attend/ignore and target-letter detection (sensory/attention task), which does not involve goal-directed problem solving or planning/sequencing operations as defined. The study does meet other inclusion criteria: I6 (whole-brain group-level fixed-effects analysis in healthy adults, n=5), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI with reported peaks), I8 (BOLD measure), and I9 (voxelwise coordinate results reported in tables). No exclusion criteria are met (E3/E4/E5/E6 not applicable). Full text appears available (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study was excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task). The task is a Moral Judgment Task requiring judgments about acceptability of actions from text scenarios (moral decision-making), which does not match the review's definition of a problem-solving task (goal-directed planning/sequencing or executing operations to arrive at a correct solution). The document does satisfy I6 (whole-brain group-level random-effects fMRI in healthy adults; n=24, ages 18–30, all male), I7 (results reported in Talairach coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI measures), and I9 (voxelwise results reported as coordinate tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore excluded for failing I5.

This task is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=22) that required participants to evaluate electrical circuit images for correctness, engaging rule-based evaluative/problem-solving processes consistent with the review’s problem-solving definition. The study reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise GLM analyses (model fit over whole brain) with results in MNI space and BOLD as the measured signal; significant contrasts (e.g., Uncertainty > Certainty, Certainty > Uncertainty, LC > OE) are reported with peak coordinates/tables. Voxelwise results are presented in tables (and discussed). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, includes within-group healthy task effects). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9 are satisfied.

This study does not examine problem-solving as defined by the review (I5 not met): the task is moral/emotional judgment (intentional vs accidental harm) rather than goal-directed problem solving, planning, or rule-based solution operations. While the report includes whole-brain BOLD results in standardized (MNI) space (I7 and I8 are met), it does not provide a whole-brain group-level task analysis specifically in a healthy adult-only sample (I6 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore excluded.

This study does not meet the review’s definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The task is an agency-inference task where participants judge whether they caused an outcome (agency experience) rather than a problem-solving paradigm requiring goal-directed planning, sequencing, evaluation, and execution to arrive at a solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level analysis, n=21 healthy adults), I7 (results reported in MNI coordinate space, reported peaks), I8 (BOLD fMRI measure), I9 (voxelwise results reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving task as defined). Exclusion criteria met: none ([]) . Full text is complete in the provided NeuroStore record for screening.

The reported task is passive viewing of a TV episode with instructions to relax/let mind wander and rate emotions; this is not a problem-solving task as defined (no goal-directed planning, evaluation, or rule-based operations). The study does include a whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults (n=11), reports coordinates in MNI space, and uses BOLD-derived connectivity measures, but it does not meet I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the paper is excluded because it fails to meet inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task).

The study used a non-verbal WCST that requires deriving and updating sorting rules via trial-and-error (inductive reasoning, feedback integration and rule-based execution), satisfying the review definition of problem solving (I5). It reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses (model fit over whole brain) on healthy adults (n=14) with group-level contrasts (within-group one-sample tests), satisfying I6. Results are given in MNI space with peak coordinates/tables (I7,I9) and the measured signal is BOLD (functional bold), satisfying I8. Thresholding and peaks are reported; no exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, includes healthy-group task effects).

The study investigated verbal fluency and causal word generation (CVF, FA, PVF) during overt word production rather than a goal-directed problem-solving task as defined by the review. Although CVF requires generating reasons, the task is essentially verbal/semantic fluency and free association under experimental instruction, not a multi-step problem with planning/sequencing or operations to reach a novel correct solution. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD results in MNI space, satisfying other inclusion criteria. Therefore I5 (problem-solving task) is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered.

The study investigates false-belief (Theory of Mind) reasoning using a cartoon task, not a problem-solving task as defined by the review (no goal-directed planning/sequencing or rule-based operations to arrive at a solution). Although the paper meets several methodological inclusion criteria (whole-brain group-level fMRI in healthy adults with reported MNI coordinates and BOLD results), it does not satisfy the core content criterion I5 (problem solving). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study is excluded.

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I5: the task is a perceptual discrimination / non-conscious visual working memory task (delayed orientation discrimination of gratings), not a problem-solving task involving goal-directed planning, sequencing, or rule-based solution generation. The document does satisfy I6 (group-level whole-brain analyses in healthy adults), I7 (results in MNI space with reported peaks), I8 (BOLD fMRI measure), and I9 (voxelwise results reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore exclusion is based on failure to meet I5 while meeting I6, I7, I8, and I9.

Exclusion E5 met: the paper reports a between-group contrast (controls > patients) and the only within-group voxelwise analysis reported is a regression conducted in patients only; no healthy-group task effect (within-subject activation in healthy adults) is reported. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported in MNI/Talairach), I8 (BOLD fMRI measure reported), I9 (voxelwise results/coordinates available). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is a Sternberg Item Recognition Task — a working memory/recognition task that does not meet the review’s problem-solving task definition), I6 (no whole-brain, group-level task effect reported for healthy adult individuals—only between-group contrast and patient-only regression). Therefore the study does not address the review objective and must be excluded.

The task requires participants to find correct associations between stimuli and actions (a clear goal) and to explore and determine the correct stimulus–response mappings, which fits the review's problem-solving definition (goal + need to figure out how to reach it; involves planning/sequencing responses and executing rule-conforming operations). The study reports whole-brain, group-level model-based fMRI analyses (model fit and inference over whole brain) in healthy adults (n=14), uses BOLD measure, reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space, and provides reported peak coordinates (tables). Thresholding and cluster details are provided. Therefore criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9 are met. No exclusion criteria apply (results are not ROI-only, not between-group only, and not non-empirical).

This study is excluded because it reports only between-group contrasts and does not report any within-group, task-related activation in healthy adults (Exclusion E5). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task is a problem-solving mental-arithmetic task), I7 (results reported in MNI space / NeuroStore indicates MNI-152 and reported peaks), I8 (BOLD measure reported), I9 (coordinate/peak results are reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no whole-brain group-level task effect reported for healthy adults — all reported analyses are between-group contrasts comparing DD and controls). Therefore it cannot be included in a meta-analysis of task-related activations in healthy adults. Full text appears complete for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study investigates probabilistic reward/value decision-making (expected value, reward magnitude, TD prediction error) rather than a problem-solving task as defined (goal-driven critical thinking, planning/sequencing to reach a correct/novel solution). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain analyses in healthy adults — several analyses report whole-brain inference; n=13 healthy adults), I7 (coordinates reported in MNI), I8 (BOLD fMRI measure), I9 (voxelwise results reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (task is reward/value choice, not a problem-solving task involving planning/sequencing/critical thinking as required). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears available in the provided NeuroStore record.

The study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria. The tasks include a deductive inference condition (DR: infer B’s hat color) that constitutes a problem-solving/logical reasoning task (I5). Analyses were whole-brain, group-level GLM with healthy adult participants (n=14) (I6). Results are reported in Talairach stereotactic space with reported peak coordinates (I7) and the measured signal is BOLD fMRI (I8). Voxelwise results are represented as reported peaks (acceptable per I9). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not limited to disease/age/gender comparisons, and include within-group healthy task effects. Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion as a task-based whole-brain fMRI investigation of problem-solving (logical inference) in healthy adults.

This study is an observational fMRI investigation in which participants watched 20-s videos of expert toolmakers and were instructed to "try to understand what the demonstrator is doing" (with Imagine and Evaluate prompts). While it reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD results in MNI coordinates (satisfying I6, I7, I8), it does not present a problem-solving task as defined by I5: participants did not engage in an explicit goal-directed problem solving activity requiring them to figure out or execute a plan or sequence of operations to reach a solution. Instead the task probes observational understanding, motor resonance, and mentalizing. No exclusion criteria are triggered (no ROI-only reporting, no disease/age/gender-only contrasts, and not a non-empirical paper), so exclusion is due to failure to meet I5. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Exclusion criteria met: none ([]).

This study does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The tasks are causal-attribution judgments (contextual vs dispositional causality) comparing causality judgments to motion-direction judgments; these involve causal inference/social-cognitive judgment rather than having a goal requiring planning/sequencing actions or executing rule-based operations to reach a solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses in healthy adults; n=15), I7 (coordinates reported in MNI), I8 (BOLD fMRI measure), I9 (voxelwise results reported as coordinates). No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, no patient-only comparisons, within-group task effects reported). Therefore the study is excluded because it fails I5 (task is not a problem-solving paradigm as defined).

This study used a theory-of-mind / false-belief story task, not a problem-solving task as defined by I5 (no goal-directed problem with planning/sequencing/executing operations to reach a solution). The paper does meet other inclusion criteria: it is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults with group-level random-effects analyses (I6), reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (I7), reports BOLD results (I8), and provides voxelwise results/peaks (I9). No exclusion criteria from the list are met. Therefore the study is excluded because it does not satisfy I5 (problem-solving task).

The study does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review. Its primary experimental manipulation is self-construal priming (task-related priming and subsequent resting-state), with a calculation condition used primarily as a control. Although simple arithmetic trials are present, the paper focuses on priming and resting-state DMN modulation rather than on a problem-solving paradigm involving goal-directed evaluation, planning/sequencing, and rule-based solution execution as the primary task contrast. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (healthy adult participants and group-level whole-brain analyses reported), I7 (results reported in MNI stereotactic space/tables), I8 (BOLD/fMRI measures reported), I9 (coordinates available in tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (study does not target a problem-solving task as the main task/contrast). No exclusion criteria from the provided list are triggered. Therefore the study is excluded on the basis that it fails to meet I5.

This study uses a two-armed bandit (reward-based choice) task examining action-value comparisons and goal-directed decision-making. It therefore meets I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI results in healthy adults), I7 (reports coordinates in MNI), I8 (BOLD analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results reported). However, it does not meet I5: the task is a reinforcement-learning/choice task (value comparison between options) rather than a problem-solving task as defined (involving evaluating a problem, planning or sequencing actions, or applying rule-based operations to reach a correct or novel solution). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Conclusion: EXCLUDED because I5 is not satisfied; inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9; inclusion criteria not met: I5; exclusion criteria met: none.

The study includes a task that meets the review’s problem-solving definition (analysis 17224409_analysis_3: mental arithmetic—silent subtraction—requires goal-directed computation and rule-based operations). It reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects BOLD analyses (model fit and inference over whole brain) with stereotactic coordinates in MNI space and tables of peaks. Participants are healthy adults (n=13–14). Therefore it satisfies I5 (problem-solving task present), I6 (whole-brain group-level effects), I7 (MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD), and I9 (coordinate results reported in tables). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not between-group-only, not patient comparisons, empirical). Full text is available in the provided NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

The study tests clinical decision-making using multiple-choice clinical questions (action-based and knowledge-based) versus control questions; this constitutes a problem-solving/decision-making task involving evaluating options and selecting actions, consistent with I5. Analyses are whole-brain (model fit and inference over whole brain) with reported stereotactic coordinates in MNI and listed peaks (I6, I7). The measure is BOLD fMRI (I8). Voxelwise results are reported as coordinate peaks/tables (I9). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only (E3), not limited to disease/age/gender comparisons (E4), include within-group task contrasts rather than only between-group contrasts (so E5 not met), and it is empirical (E6 not met). Fixed-effects group model and small sample (n=12) noted but do not violate inclusion criteria. Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

The study does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The task involved rating social scenarios for communicative versus strategic rationality rather than engaging participants in goal-directed problem solving that requires planning/sequencing actions or executing operations to reach a solution. It does meet other inclusion criteria: whole-brain task-based fMRI with group-level effects in healthy adults (I6), reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (I7), reports BOLD analyses (I8), and provides voxelwise results in tables (I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study is excluded because I5 is not satisfied.

This study does not meet the review's problem-solving task definition (I5). The reported tasks are perceptual/decision judgments (choose which object is closer; choose which person you would get along with) rather than tasks requiring goal-directed problem solving involving planning, sequencing, or executing rule-based operations to reach a (novel) solution. It does, however, meet other inclusion criteria: I6 (whole-brain, group-level random-effects fMRI analysis in healthy adults, n=24), I7 (results reported in MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI measure), and I9 (voxelwise results/peaks reported). No exclusion criteria are triggered (exclusion IDs met: none). Inclusion IDs met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion IDs not met: I5. fulltext_incomplete=false.

This fMRI study includes a calculation task that meets the review’s problem-solving definition (I5) and reports BOLD results in stereotactic (Talairach) coordinates (I7, I8, I9). However, NeuroStore indicates the model was fit over a region of interest (Model fit over: region of interest) for all analyses and results are ROI-based; no whole-brain group-level analysis is reported. Therefore it fails the requirement for at least one whole-brain analysis (I6) and meets exclusion E3 (reports only ROI results). Inclusion IDs met: I5, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion IDs not met: I6. Exclusion IDs met: E3.

This study is excluded because it reports only between-group contrasts (OCD patients > controls) and does not present group-level task activation within healthy adults, thus meeting exclusion criterion E5. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I7 (coordinates reported in MNI), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/peaks). Inclusion criteria not satisfied: I5 (task does not clearly meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task; the Iowa Gambling Task is a decision-making/uncertainty task rather than a goal-directed problem-solving task as defined), I6 (no within-healthy-group whole-brain group-level effects are reported; available analyses are between-group contrasts). No indication that the full text was unavailable. Therefore exclude.

This study examines sentence comprehension and detection of semantic illusions using true/false judgments rather than a defined problem-solving task as specified in I5. The task involves language comprehension and inference/error detection, not goal-directed problem solving that requires planning, sequencing actions, or executing rule-based operations to derive a novel solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (results reported in MNI space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise coordinate results reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (does not examine a problem-solving task as defined). No exclusion criteria are triggered (E3–E6 not met). Full text is available through the provided NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

Exclusion decision: The Stroop task used in this PET study assesses selective attention, response inhibition, and practice-dependent cognitive control rather than problem solving as defined in the review (i.e., goal-directed identification/planning/sequencing to arrive at a correct/novel solution). Exclusion IDs met: none (no exclusion criteria apply). Inclusion IDs met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates; MNI), I8 (rCBF PET measure), I9 (voxelwise results/peaks reported in tables). Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (does not study a problem-solving task per the review definition). Therefore the study is excluded for not meeting I5. Full text is complete for screening.

This study is excluded because it reports ROI-restricted inference rather than whole-brain task effects (meets exclusion E3). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (results reported in Talairach coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI measure reported), and I9 (peaks/coordinate results reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task does not clearly meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task — it is a reward-based decision-making/switching task rather than goal-directed problem solving involving planning/sequencing to reach a novel solution), and I6 (no whole-brain group-level inferences reported — inference was restricted to an ROI, so it does not provide whole-brain group effects required). Full text appears complete in the NeuroStore record. Therefore excluded on E3 with the above rationale.

This study reports a two-person choice/valuation task varying the number of available options and measures BOLD responses related to option number equality. While it meets several methodological inclusion criteria (I6: includes whole-brain group-level analyses with FWE-corrected voxelwise results; I7: reports MNI coordinates; I8: BOLD measure reported; I9: voxelwise results are reported in tables), it does NOT meet I5. The task is a valuation/decision-making paradigm about equality of choice opportunity, not a problem-solving task as defined (no goal requiring planning/sequencing operations to reach a correct or novel solution; reward probability was fixed and choices did not require rule-based problem solving). Therefore the paper should be excluded from the problem-solving meta-analysis.

The task is a Serial Reaction Time Task probing probabilistic sequential learning (procedural/sequence learning), not a problem-solving task as defined in inclusion criterion I5 (no evidence of goal-directed problem solving requiring planning/evaluative critical thinking to arrive at solutions). The study does meet other inclusion criteria: I6 (whole-brain group-level analyses in healthy adults), I7 (MNI stereotactic coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD fMRI measures), and I9 (voxelwise results available). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore excluded because I5 is not met.

This PET study tests a logical reasoning/problem-solving task (falsify conditional logical rules) in healthy adult participants and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results in MNI space for rCBF. The task fits the review’s problem-solving definition (goal-directed logical reasoning), whole-brain analyses were performed, stereotactic coordinates and peak tables are reported, and rCBF (perfusion) measures are used. Voxelwise within-group task contrasts (post>pre) and conjunction analyses are reported; results are presented as coordinates/tables. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, and includes healthy-group task effects).

The task involves rule-based arithmetic manipulation of maintained digits (apply operators indicated by cues and judge probe), which meets the review’s problem-solving definition (goal-directed, rule-based operations/planning/execution). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses were performed (model fit and inference over whole brain) in healthy adults (n=12). Results are reported as stereotactic coordinates in MNI space with peak tables (reported peaks in tbl0005). The measure is BOLD fMRI. Voxelwise results are thresholded and reported (FDR-corrected p<0.05, voxel-level), satisfying availability of coordinate results. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not patient-group comparisons only, includes within-group healthy task contrasts, empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied.

This study reports BOLD responses (I8), stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (I7), and peaks/tables of voxelwise results (I9). However, it does not provide a clear whole-brain, group-level task effect specifically in healthy adult participants (I6 not met). The whole-brain analyses appear to be performed over the combined sample or are not specified as healthy-only; many reported contrasts are between patients and controls. The task is probabilistic decision-making/judgement (JTC), which may not unambiguously meet our definition of a problem-solving task (I5 not met). Because there is no identifiable healthy-group whole-brain task effect, exclusion criterion E5 applies (includes only between-group contrasts or lacks healthy-group task effect). Thus the study is excluded.

This study does not examine a problem-solving task as defined in inclusion criterion I5. The task reported is a theory-of-mind (false belief, photo, false sign, true belief) vignette paradigm probing mentalizing/attribution of beliefs and attention, not goal-directed problem solving requiring planning, sequencing, or rule-based operations to reach a solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level analyses in healthy adults: n=21, repeated-measures random-effects, whole-brain model/inference), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported in MNI space; peaks in Table 1), I8 (BOLD fMRI measure reported), I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/peaks). Exclusion criteria met: none (does not report only ROI results, is not only group comparisons, includes within-group healthy task contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore excluded because I5 is not met.

The study investigates immediate implementation of verbally instructed stimulus-response and object-color mappings (instruction following, S-R/O-C mappings), not problem-solving as defined (goal-directed search/planning/sequencing to arrive at a novel solution). Although it reports whole-brain group BOLD results in MNI coordinates (tables) and thus meets neuroimaging reporting criteria, it does not involve critical thinking/planning or problem-solving processes required by I5. Therefore it does not meet the key content inclusion criterion.

Excluded because the reported voxelwise inference was restricted to a region-of-interest with small-volume correction (Analysis: "Inference restricted to: region of interest"), meaning the paper reports only ROI results (meets exclusion E3). The study does report BOLD data (I8), coordinates in MNI space (I7), and acceptable reporting (I9). However it does not provide a whole-brain group-level task effect with voxelwise inference across the whole brain (I6 not met). Additionally, the task is described as an executive/language Hayling Sentence Completion Test and is not clearly a problem-solving task as defined by the review (I5 not met). Therefore the study is excluded.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the review’s definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The task involves economic commitment/decision-making (accept/reject/defer prospects, bandit gamble) rather than goal-directed problem solving that requires planning/sequencing operations or applying rule-based computations to arrive at a correct solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain analyses in healthy adults: multiple whole-brain, FWE cluster-level group analyses, n=20), I7 (coordinates reported in MNI), I8 (BOLD fMRI measure), I9 (voxelwise results/peaks reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is economic decision-making, not defined problem-solving as required). Exclusion criteria met: none (no ROI-only restriction; whole-brain results are present). Full text appears complete for screening.

The study uses a reversal learning task (predicting reward/punishment for stimuli and updating responses after contingency changes), which is a reinforcement/associative learning/cognitive flexibility paradigm rather than a problem-solving task as defined by I5 (goal-directed planning, sequencing actions, and executing operations within a rule-based framework to arrive at a solution across domains). The paper does meet other inclusion criteria: whole-brain group-level fMRI analysis in healthy adults (I6), stereotactic coordinates reported in MNI space (I7), reports BOLD results (I8), and coordinate reporting is available in tables (I9). No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore excluded because it does not meet I5 (problem-solving task).

The task is a moral judgment task involving evaluating dilemmas and making appropriateness judgments; it does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The study does satisfy other methodological criteria: whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses (I6), reports stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space (I7), uses BOLD fMRI (I8), and provides voxelwise results in reported tables (I9). No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., results are not ROI-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Therefore exclude because inclusion criterion I5 is not met.

This task involves verification of two-operation arithmetic problems combined with working memory retention, which fits the meta-analysis definition of problem solving (goal-directed arithmetic operations within a rule set). The study used task-based fMRI with BOLD measure, whole-brain model fitting (MNI coordinate space), and reports group-level voxelwise results (within-group and random-effects contrasts, corrected and uncorrected thresholds) with stereotactic peaks/tables. Participants are healthy adults. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, patient-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met.

Excluded because the reported analyses are ROI-based (model fit over: region of interest; regions defined a priori in striatum) and no whole-brain group-level voxelwise analysis is reported, violating I6 and triggering exclusion E3. The task is a reinforcement-learning/stimulus-action-reward association learning task, not a problem-solving task as defined (I5 not met). The study does report BOLD measures and stereotactic coordinates (MNI) and coordinate reporting is acceptable. Inclusion criteria met: I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criteria not met: I5, I6. Exclusion criteria met: E3.

The study uses a mental-rotation task in healthy adults (n=10) that requires a goal (judge stimulus parity) and mental transformations to reach the correct response, which fits the review's definition of a problem-solving task. It reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD analyses (GLM/ANCOVA) with inference over the whole brain; the coordinate space is MNI and reported peaks (3) are listed in a table; a BOLD measure is used. These satisfy inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are whole-brain rather than ROI-only, the sample are healthy adults, and this is an empirical within-group task effect. Note: sample size is small (n=10), but this does not violate the stated inclusion/exclusion criteria.

The study uses a mental rotation task (Shepard–Metzler figures) which is a visuospatial transformation/same–different judgment rather than a multi-step problem-solving paradigm as defined by I5 (goal-directed evaluation, planning/sequencing actions, and executing rule-based operations to reach a previously unknown solution). While the task requires mental transformation, it does not match the review's operational definition of problem solving. The manuscript does meet other inclusion criteria: whole-brain group-level analyses are reported (I6), coordinate space is MNI with stereotactic peak tables (I7/I9), and the measure is BOLD fMRI (I8). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore the study is excluded because it does not satisfy I5 (problem-solving task).

The study reports task-based fMRI (BOLD) data collected during tasks that include classic problem-solving/fluid-reasoning tasks (Matrix reasoning, Paper folding, Letter sets) that meet the review's problem-solving definition. Analyses were whole-brain (model fit over whole brain), group-level within-subject task effects are reported (simple effects with peak coordinates in tables), and coordinate space is MNI. The sample is healthy adults (n=174) screened to exclude dementia/MCI. The report includes voxelwise peak tables (reported peaks for each contrast). Therefore it satisfies I5 (problem-solving tasks), I6 (whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (coordinates in MNI), I8 (BOLD analyses), and I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not only group comparisons, includes healthy-group task effects, empirical human data).

The study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for the review. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (analyses are region-of-interest only; model fit and inference are restricted to an ROI/SPM mask) and E5 (study includes only Parkinson's disease patients and reports no healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (coordinates reported in MNI space) and I9 (voxelwise peaks reported in a table). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task does not clearly meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task — contrasts labeled CRT/SUB suggest reaction-time measures, not problem solving), I6 (participants are patients with Parkinson's disease, not healthy adults), and I8 (measure is molecular tracer uptake—PET tracer uptake—not BOLD or rCBF). Given ROI-only inference and absence of healthy adult task-based whole-brain results, the study is not eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This study is an fMRI BOLD whole-brain group analysis in healthy adults (n=9) reporting results in MNI space, so it meets I6, I7, I8, and I9. However, the task is a numerosity/magnitude comparison (compare number of dots vs color judgment), which is a perceptual/discrimination task and does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5) requiring goal-directed planning, sequencing, or executing rule-based operations to reach a solution. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task).

Exclusion decision rationale: This study does not meet inclusion criterion I5. The task is a Theory of Mind false-belief task (processing incongruent mental states), not a problem-solving task defined as goal-directed problem-solving involving planning/sequencing operations to reach a solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analysis in healthy adults), I7 (results reported in MNI space), I8 (BOLD fMRI measure), I9 (voxelwise results reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not a problem-solving task). Exclusion criteria met: none (E3–E6 not applicable). Full text completeness: fulltext_incomplete=false. Given the clear mismatch with the core review objective (I5), the study must be excluded.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria. The task is an explicit action-planning task (goal cue vs. grip cue) requiring participants to plan/sequence object-directed actions to achieve a goal, which satisfies the problem-solving definition (I5). It reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects fMRI analyses in healthy adults (n=16) (I6). Results are reported in stereotactic space (MNI) with peak coordinates (I7). The measure is BOLD functional response (I8). The NeuroStore record documents voxelwise whole-brain contrasts and reported peaks/tables, which satisfies acceptability of reported coordinates (I9). No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are whole-brain (not ROI-only), the study is empirical and includes healthy-group task effects. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study must be excluded because it does not study a problem-solving task as defined in the review (I5 not met). The task used is an Anti-Saccade Task (response inhibition/error processing), which does not meet the review's definition of problem solving (having a goal and requiring planning/sequencing critical-thinking operations to arrive at a solution). The paper does satisfy other inclusion criteria: I6 (whole-brain, group-level effects in healthy adults are reported), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported in Talairach), I8 (BOLD/fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise peaks reported in a table). No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., results are whole-brain, include within-group healthy effects). fulltext_incomplete is false.

Excluded because the task (feedback-guided reversal learning) is a reinforcement/associative learning and decision-making paradigm rather than a problem-solving task as defined in I5 (no evidence of goal-directed planning, sequencing of actions or rule-based problem solving to arrive at a novel solution). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults), I7 (results reported in MNI stereotactic space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), I9 (coordinate results reported). Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving task per the review definition).

(a) Exclusion criteria met: E5 — the reported whole-brain contrasts are omnibus between-group tests and the paper does not report a healthy-group task effect (analyses are described as between-group/interaction contrasts and ROI group comparisons). (b) Inclusion criteria met: I7 (results in MNI coordinate space reported), I8 (BOLD/fMRI measure reported), I9 (voxelwise peak coordinates reported in tables). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I5 — task is conditioning/reinforcement, not a problem-solving task as defined; I6 — no clear whole-brain group-level task effect reported for healthy adults (only between-group omnibus contrasts). Therefore the study is excluded.

This is an event-related, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=16) that investigates transitive inference/relational reasoning—a logical problem-solving task requiring integration of relations to reach a conclusion, which fits the review’s definition of problem solving (I5). The report includes whole-brain group-level GLM analyses (model fit over whole brain; group-level t tests) and BOLD measures (I6,I8). Results are reported as stereotactic coordinates in MNI space and peaks/tables are provided (I7,I9). No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are not limited to ROIs, are within healthy-group task effects, and the paper is empirical.

The study used a mental arithmetic (algebraic) task requiring participants to compute and select correct solutions, which meets the review's problem-solving definition (I5). It reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects GLM analyses in healthy adults (n=22; ages 18–24) (I6). Results are reported in MNI space with tables of peak coordinates (I7, I9), and the neuroimaging measure is BOLD fMRI (I8). Multiple whole-brain within-group contrasts are reported (e.g., High Effort>Low Effort, Big Reward>Small Reward), so voxelwise task effects in healthy participants are available. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, not only between-group or subgroup comparisons). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

Excluded because the reported analyses are ROI-based with no clear whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (Analysis 0 explicitly ROI; Analysis 1 lacks features indicating whole-brain analysis). This meets exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI results). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (coordinates reported in MNI), I8 (BOLD measure reported), and I9 (peaks/coordinate results are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is a perceptual/reward estimation decision task, not a problem-solving task as defined), and I6 (no evidence of at least one whole-brain group-level analysis). Therefore the study does not satisfy all required inclusion criteria for the review and must be excluded.

This study does not meet inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task). The task is decision-making under risk (affect-rich vs affect-poor choices/lotteries), not a problem-solving paradigm involving planning/sequencing actions to reach a goal or executing rule-based operations to derive a solution. The record does satisfy I6 (whole-brain, group-level analyses in healthy adults), I7 (coordinates reported in MNI), I8 (BOLD/fMRI measure), and I9 (coordinate tables reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the paper must be excluded because it fails to meet all required inclusion criteria (specifically I5).

This study is excluded because it does not examine task-based problem solving in healthy adults. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (study does not include any healthy-group task effect; participants are methamphetamine-dependent patients and the paradigm is a resting-state scan). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (results reported in MNI coordinate space), I8 (BOLD functional connectivity measure reported), I9 (voxelwise results/peaks reported in tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not a task-based problem solving paradigm; task is resting-state with eyes open), I6 (does not include healthy adult group-level task effects; participants are patients). Fulltext is complete for screening. Given these mismatches with the review objective (task-based problem solving in healthy adults), the paper must be excluded.

The study uses a mental rotation task (same/different judgments on rotated images of hands and tools), which is a visuospatial transformation task rather than a problem-solving task as defined by I5 (involving evaluation, planning/sequencing actions, and executing rule-based operations to reach a solution). The record meets other inclusion criteria: whole-brain group analyses in healthy adults (I6), reported stereotactic coordinates in Talairach (I7), BOLD measure reported (I8), and coordinate tables provided (I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore excluded because it does not meet I5.

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I5 (task is moral judgment of scenarios, not a problem-solving task as defined). It does meet I6 (whole-brain, group-level random-effects analysis in healthy adults, n=29), I7 (reports coordinates in MNI space; reported peaks), I8 (BOLD fMRI measure), and I9 (voxelwise results reported). No exclusion criteria are met (E3–E6 not applicable). Therefore the paper is excluded for failing to satisfy I5 (problem-solving task).

The study reports an fMRI task (hierarchical rule task) involving goal-directed, rule-based selection from working memory consistent with problem-solving operations (planning/sequencing and rule-based execution) satisfying I5. It includes a whole-brain, group-level mixed-effects analysis in healthy adults (n=22) with model fit and inference over the whole brain (I6). Coordinates are reported in MNI space with reported peaks (I7). The measure is BOLD response (I8). Coordinate results are available as reported peaks (I9). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not limited to ROIs (not E3), not only group comparisons of disease/age/gender (not E4), includes within-group task effects (not E5), and it is empirical human data (not E6). Full text appears available in the NeuroStore record. Overall, the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective of whole-brain task-based fMRI studies of problem solving in healthy adults.

The study uses a moral judgment (theory-of-mind) task rather than a problem-solving paradigm as defined by the review. It therefore fails inclusion criterion I5 (task is not a problem-solving task). It does meet I6 (whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD measure), and I9 (voxelwise results reported). No exclusion criteria apply. Exclude because I5 is not satisfied; other inclusion criteria are satisfied.

This study is an fMRI investigation of metaphor/conceptual expansion (creative cognition) using passive judgments of unusualness and appropriateness, not a goal-directed problem-solving task as defined (I5 not met). Analyses were conducted within predefined ROIs (model fit over region of interest; regions listed), and NeuroStore reports ROI-based results only, so it violates the whole-brain requirement (E3 applies) and thus fails I6. The study does report stereotactic coordinates in MNI space and BOLD measures (I7 and I8 met) and voxelwise results are reported in tables (I9 met). Conclusion: EXCLUDE because E3 is met and key inclusion criteria I5 and I6 are not met.

This study examines implicit false-belief (theory-of-mind) processing using Sally-Anne-style tasks and true/false judgments; it does not involve a problem-solving task as defined by I5 (no goal-oriented planning, sequencing actions, or rule-based operations to arrive at a solution). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults), I7 (coordinates reported in Talairach space), I8 (BOLD measure reported), I9 (voxelwise results/peaks reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is ToM/false-belief, not problem-solving). No exclusion criteria from the list apply (exclusion_criteria_applied = []). Full text is complete for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study investigates moral evaluation/social cognition (justice sensitivity, praise/blame) rather than a problem-solving task as defined (goal-directed planning/sequencing to reach a solution). Although it contains whole-brain group-level BOLD analyses reported in MNI space (satisfying I6, I7, I8, and I9), it does not meet I5 (task is not a problem-solving paradigm). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the paper is excluded for failing to meet inclusion criterion I5.

This study does not meet I5 (problem-solving task). The task involved passive presentation of digits and number words with attention/foot-pedal checks and instruction to avoid movement; there is no goal-directed problem-solving, planning, or execution of rule-based operations to reach a solution. It does meet I6 (whole-brain group-level analyses in healthy adults; n=29), I7 (reports coordinates in MNI), I8 (BOLD fMRI measure), and I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables). No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study is excluded because inclusion criterion I5 is not satisfied (other inclusion criteria I6, I7, I8, I9 are satisfied; exclusion IDs met: none).

This study does not examine a problem-solving task as defined in inclusion criterion I5. It investigates Theory of Mind / pragmatic language (false-belief and coherent story comprehension), not goal-directed problem solving involving planning/sequencing or rule-based operations to reach a solution. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI), I8 (BOLD fMRI measure reported), I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables). Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving paradigm). fulltext_incomplete: false.

The paper uses a sentence-completion (Hayling) task and reports BOLD results in Talairach coordinates (I7, I8 met) with peaks in tables (I9 met). However, the task is not clearly a problem-solving task as defined (I5 not met). Crucially, all reported analyses are between-group contrasts (controls vs. high-risk subgroups or patient subgroup comparisons) and no within-group, healthy adult task-related activation is reported; thus the study includes only between-group contrasts and does not provide a healthy-group task effect (violates inclusion I6 and meets exclusion E5). The reported results focus on disease-related group comparisons, satisfying exclusion E4 as well. Therefore the study must be excluded.

The study reports task-based fMRI BOLD data during explicit reasoning/problem-solving tasks (forced-choice problems with tourist cities and U.S. states), satisfying I5. Multiple second-level, group-level whole-brain analyses are reported (model fit over whole brain; participants treated as random effects), satisfying I6. Coordinates are reported in ICBM152 stereotactic space (MNI-like), satisfying I7. The measure is BOLD (functional bold), satisfying I8. Voxelwise peaks and tables are reported (reported peaks, Tables t1–t3), satisfying I9. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only (there are whole-brain contrasts), the sample is healthy adult participants (n=16), and the paper is empirical. Therefore the article meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis.

The study does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined in inclusion criterion I5. It is an fMRI study of observing joint actions and shared intentions (social cognition), with tasks involving tracking intentions or colored dots, not goal-directed problem solving, planning, or rule-based solution operations. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level random-effects analysis in healthy adults), I7 (results reported in MNI space), I8 (BOLD fMRI measure reported), I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving task). No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only reporting, no between-group-only contrasts, empirical healthy adult task effects present). fulltext_incomplete=false

Excluded because it does not include any whole-brain, group-level task effects in healthy adults (E5). The study is a single-case (n=1) clinical patient (age 15) with a history of brain tumor and radiation-induced white-matter damage; the reported task is verb generation (not a problem-solving task). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported in Talairach; reported peaks = 2), I8 (BOLD/fMRI measure reported), I9 (voxelwise peaks/coordinates reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task does not qualify as a problem-solving task as defined), I6 (no whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adult individuals; sample is a single patient). No other exclusion criteria apply. Full text is complete for screening.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment in healthy adults where participants silently read sentences and decide whether described volleyball actions are technically feasible — an evaluative decision task that entails critical thinking and evaluation consistent with the review's definition of problem solving (I5). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level analyses (flexible factorial and conjunction analyses) with inference over the whole brain (I6), provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space with reported peak tables (I7, I9), and uses BOLD fMRI measures (I8).
