There are task>rest and stimulus contrasts showing within-group task effects, so it is not limited to between-group contrasts or ROI-only results. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) appear to apply. Full text completeness: the NeuroStore record provided is sufficient for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false).

Although this fMRI study meets several methodological inclusion criteria (whole-brain group analyses in healthy adults with BOLD measures reported in MNI space), it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review. The task is a Stroop Color-Word conflict paradigm (response selection/attention/conflict resolution), not a goal-directed problem-solving task that requires evaluating the problem, planning/sequencing actions, or executing operations to arrive at a correct or novel solution. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (study of a problem solving task) is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria are triggered (no ROI-only reporting, not a patient-group comparison only, contains healthy-group task effects, and is empirical).

The Mental Clock Test requires participants to determine whether the angle between clock hands is <90° or >90°. This entails a clear goal and mental manipulation/operation applying a rule to arrive at a correct judgement, consistent with the review's definition of problem-solving (evaluating/planning/performing operations to reach a correct solution). The study reports whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses (one-sample t-tests, n=20 healthy adults) with BOLD as the measure, uses Talairach stereotactic space, and provides coordinate tables. Voxelwise results and thresholds are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not patient-group-only, not non-empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied.

This study investigates intention understanding of observed gestures, not problem-solving as defined by the review (no goal-directed problem solving, planning/sequencing, or rule-based solution operations). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level random-effects analyses reported: Analyses 1 and 2 infer over whole brain), I7 (coordinates reported in MNI), I8 (BOLD fMRI measure), I9 (voxelwise results reported via tables). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (task is action/ intention inference, not a problem-solving task). No exclusion criteria are triggered (E3–E6 not met). Therefore excluded for failing I5.

This study used a perceptual causality judgment task (participants judged whether one ball caused another to move) rather than a goal-directed problem-solving task. Inclusion criterion I5 (task-based study of problem solving involving goal-directed planning/sequencing or rule-based operations to arrive at a solution) is not satisfied. The study does satisfy I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses reported), I7 (results reported in MNI stereotactic space with peak coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI measure), and I9 (voxelwise results/peaks reported in tables). No exclusion criteria apply: it is not ROI-only (E3), not limited to disease/age/gender comparisons (E4), includes within-group healthy task effects (so E5 not met), and is empirical (E6 not met). Therefore exclude due to failure to meet I5 (problem-solving definition).

The study is an event-related, whole-brain BOLD fMRI investigation in healthy adults (n=24) reporting MNI coordinates and group-level random-effects contrasts, so it meets I6, I7, I8, and I9. However, the task is financial decision-making under risk influenced by expert advice (choices between sure-win and lottery offers) rather than a defined problem-solving task as specified by I5. The paradigm does not involve goal-directed problem decomposition, planning/sequencing of actions, rule-based operations to arrive at a correct solution, or explicit critical thinking processes required by the review definition of problem solving. No exclusion criteria are triggered. Therefore the paper is excluded for failing to meet I5 (problem-solving task).

This study is excluded because it does not examine problem-solving in healthy adults. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (Includes only between-group contrasts or doesn't include any healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in Talairach), I8 (reports BOLD measure), I9 (coordinates/peaks reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (does not appear to study a problem-solving task as defined; tasks are reward/value choice, oddball, working memory, sensorimotor, and recall, which do not meet the specified problem-solving definition), I6 (does not include whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adult individuals; participants listed are patients with cocaine dependence, schizophrenia, or Alzheimer's disease, with no healthy-group task effects reported). Full text is available in the provided document representation, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study includes a classic problem-solving task (Wisconsin Card Sorting Task) in a free-choice version requiring rule identification and rule-based responding, which fits the review’s problem-solving definition (I5). It reports whole-brain, group-level fMRI results (model fit and inference over whole brain) in healthy adults (n=15) satisfying I6. Results are reported in MNI space with peak coordinate tables (I7), BOLD responses are the measured neural signal (I8), and voxelwise results are provided in tables (I9). No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are whole-brain (not ROI-only), involve healthy-group task effects, and are empirical. Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

The study uses a visual lexical/number recognition task (same/different judgments on character strings), not a problem-solving task as defined. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level random-effects analysis in healthy adults; n=20), I7 (results reported in MNI stereotactic space with peak coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI measure), I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (task-based study of problem solving — the task lacks goal-directed problem solving, planning, or rule-based solution operations as defined). No exclusion criteria apply (E3-E6 none met). Therefore the paper is excluded for failing I5.

This study reports a card-guessing (gambling) task comparing risk estimation and feedback processing in children and adults. It includes whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults (n=14), reports stereotactic Talairach coordinates (tables), and uses BOLD measures. However, the task is a decision-making/gambling paradigm, not a problem-solving task as defined (goal-directed problem solving involving critical evaluation, planning/sequencing actions, and rule-based operations to arrive at solutions). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task) is not met, so the study must be excluded.

This study is excluded because it is a resting-state, seed-based connectivity study in nicotine-dependent patients (not healthy adults) and reports only region-of-interest (ROI) analyses. It does not investigate a problem-solving task (I5 not met), does not include healthy adult task-based whole-brain group effects (I6 not met), and does not report task-related activation results relevant to problem solving (I7 not met). It does report BOLD connectivity measures (I8 met), but the analyses were ROI-restricted and in a patient sample. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (ROI-only results) and E5 (no healthy-group task effect / only patient group). Inclusion criteria met: I8. Inclusion criteria not met: I5, I6, I7, I9.

This study is excluded because it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review (I5 not met). It is an fMRI study of reciprocity in a Trust Game (social decision-making), not a goal-directed problem-solving paradigm requiring planning/sequencing to arrive at a correct solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates; MNI space; peaks reported), I8 (BOLD fMRI measures), I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables). Exclusion criteria met: none (no ROI-only reporting; within-group task contrasts present). Full text completeness: sufficient for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study should be excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I5: the reported task is an instrumental reversal/reward-learning task (updating choices based on reward prediction errors), which is a reward-based decision-making paradigm rather than a problem-solving task as defined (goal-directed critical thinking, planning/sequencing operations within semantic/algebraic/logical/mechanical frameworks to reach a correct solution). The record does satisfy I6 (includes whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults) and I8 (reports BOLD analyses). The record does not explicitly report stereotactic coordinates in the provided document, so I7 is not met based on this document. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered by the available information.

The task is a moral-judgment trolley-dilemma task rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (no evidence participants engaged in planning/sequencing actions or executing rule-based operations to reach a goal). All analyses report inference restricted to a region-of-interest using small-volume correction (ROI-only inference), so whole-brain voxelwise inference/results are not reported. Exclusion applied: E3 (reports only ROI results). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (results reported in MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (coordinate results are reported/available). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not a problem-solving task per review definition), I6 (does not provide whole-brain group-level inference/results). Full text is complete in this NeuroStore-derived record (fulltext_incomplete=false).
